subject: general
question: According to the Economic Survey 2025, what was the unemployment rate in India for 2023-24?
solution:
The correct answer is 3__**.2%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **According to the Economic Survey 2025**, the **unemployment rate **in India for the financial year** 2023-24 **was recorded at **3.2%**.
 
• This is a significant improvement compared to earlier years, indicating **better employment opportunities and economic recovery** post-pandemic.
 
• The data in the Economic Survey is based on the **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)**, which is conducted by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).
 
• The unemployment rate measures the percentage of people in the labor force who are willing to work but are unable to find jobs.
 
• A lower unemployment rate is often seen as an indicator of a growing and stable economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS):**

 
 
• Introduced in 2017 by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) to provide reliable employment and unemployment data.
 
• It measures key labor market indicators such as Worker Population Ratio (WPR), Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), and Unemployment Rate (UR).
 
• The PLFS is conducted quarterly in urban areas and annually in rural areas.
 
 
 
• **Unemployment Rate:**
 
 
• The unemployment rate is calculated as the ratio of the number of unemployed individuals to the total labor force, expressed as a percentage.
 
• It is a critical indicator of economic health and reflects the availability of jobs in the economy.
 
• Factors influencing unemployment include economic growth, industrial development, and government policies.
 
 
 
• **Impact of COVID-19 on Employment:**
 
 
• The pandemic initially caused widespread job losses, especially in sectors like hospitality, tourism, and retail.
 
• However, government initiatives such as Atmanirbhar Bharat and Make in India have helped boost job creation and economic recovery.
 
 
 
• **Government Measures to Reduce Unemployment:**
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY):** Aims to provide skill training to increase employability.
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA):** Provides guaranteed wage employment to rural households.
 
• **Start-Up India:** Encourages entrepreneurship and innovation to generate employment.
